indexes._comment: My Experiments / Trash: where ownerId == me && trash == ? orderBy updatedAt desc
Recent: where visibility == 'public' && trash == false orderBy createdAt desc
Showcase home: where sourceType == 'video' && ownerId == 'system' orderBy createdAt desc
Related: where recordingId == X && visibility in [public,unlisted]
Raw: where ownerId == me && isRaw == true (isRaw boolean mirrors segments==null, since composite indexes can't equality-match an array field)
Admin moderation queue: where status == 'open' orderBy createdAt desc
Reports on one panorama, newest first (admin detail + closing them out on delete)
Admin: panoramas auto-hidden by reports, newest first (also the bulk-restore list after a report-bombing)

fieldOverrides._comment: Settings profile card: count comments authored by me across all experiments (collectionGroup query on senderId)
My Classes: find a student's joined classes via collectionGroup('members') where uid == me

Account deletion: a user's submissions across every class (collectionGroup('submissions') where studentUid == me) — including classes they have since left, where the membership doc is gone but the submission remains
Account deletion: a user's grades across every class (collectionGroup('grades') where studentUid == me)

Account deletion: a user's private workspace items across every class (collectionGroup('workspace') where studentUid == me). The COLLECTION entry preserves the automatic single-field index the class page's own workspace query relies on — a field override replaces automatic indexing for that field
Account deletion: work promoted to a class showcase that belongs to a user (collectionGroup('showcase') where ownerUid == me)

Account deletion: entries in OTHER users' block lists that point at the account being deleted (collectionGroup('blocks') where authorId == me). Without this the deleted account's id would survive as a bare string in strangers' block lists

Not indexed: the follow-ups kept on an open report (functions/src/moderation.ts appendFollowUp) are an array of maps carrying up to 10 × 500 characters of free text, and nothing queries any of it — the admin page reads the whole report document. Automatic indexing would write an index entry per map field per follow-up for no reader. Account deletion's own queries on this collection (reporterId / svOwnerId / expOwnerId / authorId, plain equality) are served by the automatic single-field indexes and are deliberately NOT overridden anywhere in this file. This exemption is an optimisation, not a prerequisite — 500 characters is far under Firestore's index-entry limit, so nothing fails without it — and it can be applied on its own with `gcloud firestore indexes fields update --collection-group=streetviewReports --field-path=followUps --disable-indexes`, which is the safer route: deploying this whole file would also create the TTL policies declared below that are not live yet

TTL: street view reports are deleted 12 months after filing (privacy policy §5). The TTL entries below were enabled with gcloud on 2026-09-14 and are recorded here so an indexes deploy leaves them alone — a TTL field missing from this file is offered for deletion, and --force deletes it. Their indexes are the inherited defaults, listed only so the override matches what is live
TTL: reporter rate-limit buckets, about a day after the last report (privacy policy §1.8, §5)
TTL: the global auto-hide circuit breaker counter (no personal data)
TTL: one-staff-mail-per-hour throttle, keyed by the reported panorama or author
TTL: contact-form IP hash, two hours after the last message (privacy policy §1.6, §5)
TTL: view-counting hash, two hours after the last counted view (privacy policy §1.6, §5)
TTL: website error reports, 90 days (privacy policy §1.6, §5)

TTL: AI report flags, 12 months after filing (privacy policy §1.8). This entry and the two AI counters below come from app repo docs/proposals/ai-open-access.md §3.8 and were not yet live when they were added
TTL: the daily AI report total across personal accounts, 8 days after its UTC day starts (no personal data)
TTL: per-account AI report counters, about 26 hours after the last report (privacy policy §1.5)
